analysis.title: GS Consumer: Glass Full (Feiler) 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Consumer stocks traded well on the day after earnings. TGT was +6% and TJX +10% on 18 Nov. VIK was +4% the day before and +7% on 18 Nov.

Investors' initial feedback found holes in all three prints: TGT's 4Q guide and soft apparel comps, a TJX gross margin miss, and an outright VIK miss with a cut for 2027. The stocks still traded higher.
The macro backdrop helped, with UST yields down about 5 bps and CL1 down 4%.
The size factor drove many of the moves. GS's consumer large vs small basket (GSCNSIZE Index) was down 60 bps, most visibly in restaurants, which is prompting questions in the sector.
WMT and WSM report earnings on 19 Nov. Investors widely expect WSM to beat on both the top and bottom line.
WMT is the print to watch, mainly for read-across to peers. Almost everyone GS has heard from is at +3% WMT US comps, give or take 30 bps.

The bigger WMT debate is price investments. Last quarter WMT said it would lean in heavily on prices. Investors said during the quarter that it backed off that approach, which helped sentiment for Food Retail.
TPR is flat on the day and has given back almost all of its +7% earnings-day move. Investors are split on whether a promo launched 18 Nov is new or the same as last year's.
WING is lagging the strength elsewhere in restaurants, with a data focus (still soft).
DG has lagged DLTR for a second day. GS thinks DG is more owned and defensives lag, and some feedback said recent boutique checks were more positive on DLTR.

TJX reported a gross margin miss. The stock was +10% on 18 Nov.
VIK reported an outright miss and cut its 2027 outlook. The stock was +4% the day before and +7% on 18 Nov.
WMT reports 19 Nov. Investor expectations for WMT US comps are about +3%, give or take 30 bps (expectation, not a print).
WSM reports 19 Nov. Investors widely expect a beat on top and bottom line (expectation, not a print).
TPR gave back almost all of its +7% earnings-day move.

Lower oil was a macro tailwind for consumer stocks on the day.
Investor positioning is near +3%, so modest upside is the bar and the read on price investments matters more.

Size-factor rotation can drive stock moves independent of earnings.
